Priya,

Quick update from our side: Procurement is running a formal bakeoff against two vendors next month. One is a large cloud provider offering an integrated stack and a pretty aggressive price/modeling proposal; the other is an inference-optimized vendor who claims 2–3x lower token costs on our average workloads (they've shared a short benchmark).

Jordan and I are still in favor of keeping things with Redwood (runtime stability and support have been great), but procurement is pushing for a reduced unit cost and longer committed term if they switch. They asked for a detailed cost breakdown, any benchmark artifacts we can provide, and a concrete counterproposal by next Tuesday (23 Feb).

Can you send over:
- A concise comparison (tokens / request profile / expected monthly cost at current vs proposed terms)
- Any performance notes we can share from our production telemetry (latency p95, concurrency behavior)
- A pragmatic save plan (credits, term/commit options, Dedicated capacity offer)

Thanks — want to be transparent so you have time to put something together.

Alex
Director of ML Systems
SignalWorks

Folks — forwarding Alex's note. SignalWorks is a mid-market customer (~$220k ARR) up for renewal in April. Procurement wants a formal cost comparison and a counteroffer by next week.

Key asks: benchmark artifacts, clear price math, and a short save plan we can present. I think we should propose:
- 12% renewal credit applied to year 1 invoice if they commit to 24 months, OR
- Dedicated burst pool + 10% committed discount for a 12-month term (they care about predictable throughput for their search feature), OR
- Proof-of-performance window: 30-day dedicated test environment with telemetry and a success SLT (p95 latency <= 400ms at their profile) and a $X credit on conversion to a full term.

Neha — can you produce the perf slice and a short one-page benchmark explanation we can share? Rishi — pricing ask: run the math for 12, 24, 36 month commitments including our Dedicated uplift and what margin floors look like. I attached a template for the cost comparison.

We should keep the customer-facing doc concise (1–2 pages) and put the detailed workbook in HubSpot.

Thanks — will sync 10:30am tomorrow if that works.

Priya

Team — attaching the prod telemetry snapshot and a short explainer. Highlights from the last 90 days (sample = 2.1M generation calls):
- Avg tokens per call: 84
- Token reuse/prefix cache hit: 28% (common prefixes in search reranks)
- p50 latency: 88ms, p95: 362ms (at observed concurrency peaks)
- Sustained throughput: 4800 tokens/sec across their fleet with our default batching profile

Bench note: the competitor's public benchmark shows lower per-token cost by aggressively quantizing and restricting burst concurrency; in our internal tests those savings are real but rely on increased tail latency and a 15–20% fail-rate under the SignalWorks profile (their dataset includes many long-form re-ranks). We should call that out — the tradeoff is lower per-unit cost vs. degraded SLT and potential error surface for their latency-sensitive search use-case.

Attaching: 20270218-signalworks-telemetry.csv (referenced in the workbook).

Neha

Subject: SignalWorks renewal counterproposal and practical save plan

Alex / Jordan — thanks again for the transparency and for sharing the procurement timelines. Per our discussion, please find our concise counterproposal and short save plan below. I'm happy to schedule a 30-minute procurement review next week to walk through the numbers.

Summary (two-minute read):
- What SignalWorks told us: procurement needs a lower unit cost or stronger committed terms to avoid switching.
- What Redwood offers (options):
  1) Financial-first: 12% one-time renewal credit applied to year-1 invoice + standard support. 24-month minimum term. No Dedicated uplift.
  2) Performance-first: 10% committed discount + Dedicated burst pool (guaranteed baseline throughput with burst capacity) for 12 months. Includes instrumentation dashboard and 30-day proof-of-performance with pass criteria (p95 <= 400ms at your observed profile).
  3) PoP-to-convert: 30-day dedicated evaluation (reduced test rate) with full telemetry. If SignalWorks converts to a 24-month committed term within 15 days after PoP, we apply a $22,000 conversion credit to the first invoice.

Benchmarks & risk notes (excerpt):
- Our 90-day production slice indicates p95 ~362ms at observed concurrency; we see stable behavior across heavy re-rank workloads.
- Competitor tradeoff: lower unit cost observed at the expense of increased p95 and higher request fails under long-tail workloads. We believe that undermines search quality. We can provide a side-by-side token-cost comparison and the telemetry slice for procurement to validate.

Suggested next steps:
1) Choose preferred option (1, 2, or 3) — we can finalize pricing table and DocuSign by Thurs (25 Feb).
2) If you want Performance-first (Option 2), we’ll stand up the 30-day PoP within 5 business days of agreement.
3) We’ll post the detailed workbook to HubSpot and provide a short one-page exec summary for procurement.

Attachments: one-page counterproposal (save-plan-draft-20270222.pdf) and cost comparison workbook (20270222-signalworks-cost-comparison.xlsx). HubSpot link with full workbook: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/123456/company/SignalWorks (doc in deals tab). DocuSign link will be ready once you pick an option.

If you prefer I can jump on a call Wednesday at 11am PT — CC'd are my Solutions and Engineering leads if procurement wants to speak to tradeoffs live.

Best,
Priya Natarajan
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
